items.note: "which is what a lookup yields for a key with no value in the map" is a bit ambiguous: `default` is only consulted by the inherited `apply`/`applyOrElse` (e.g. `props("x")`), not by `get`, which this class overrides separately to return `None` for a missing key. A reader could conflate the two. Consider "...which `apply` returns for a key with no value in the map" for precision. Not a blocker since the base `scala.collection.Map#default` doc uses similarly loose phrasing ("returned when a key is not found").
`@return `Some` result of `body`, or `None` if...` reads a little awkwardly ("Some result of body" vs. the intended "the result of `body`, wrapped in `Some`"). Minor wording polish only.
